"us against them", the idea that no one is innocent, completely trashing "protect and serve" in favor of "track and intimidate". Blaming this cop will not fix the problem. Better internal investigations will only mitigate the symptom. We need a strong nationwide push from inside police departments to start serving and protecting again. And one look at forums made for and by cops to talk to each-other will tell you that's going to be a huge culture change.

"Protect and serve" is not what the cops in America are for, and it never has been, at least not in terms of protecting and serving the people.

Municipal police forces were first developed in America to protect mercantile interests as population density increased in major ports of trade. And when you think about the history of policing in the Southern states, which began as organized Slave Patrols, "track and intimidate" is actually a far more accurate description of the tradition.

The only history I could find on the phrase "Protect and serve" is from Los Angeles Police Department's motto.

I think it's pretty clear when the phrase "Protect and Serve" is ever brought up in any conversation regarding police, it's pejorative because it's widely understood that this public-relations-based "promise" has never actually been delivered anywhere.

This attitude is encouraged by giving them military hardware, hiring war veterans, and creating bad training.

I believe they want everyone to hate police so that the idea of federalizing/privatizing police sounds good. I think it's happening partly on its own, but I think they've given it quite a big push, too.

There is such a thing as traumatic amnesia, but this isn't it. He knows what he did, and so do his fellow policemen. They're all covering his ass and playing our legal system by pretending to not know something they obviously know.
It doesn't work for suspects, it shouldn't work for cops.

I wanted to make a quick Sigil Creation Guide for those of you that may be interested in starting. I've outlined the bare minimum of how I believe they work best for me and adding a good bit of info from previous threads and infographics here. Enjoy!

In my own opinion, here is how a sigil works for the user, and how I envision them working for me

  1. Utilize the Grant Morrison sigil creation method by making an intent, removing vowels, eliminating doubled consonants, and molding it into a symbol.
  2. Make sure you understand how intents work. It's very literal. "Don't / want / etc," force those intents on you. "I Am, I have, I will" are all very powerful phrases in order.
  3. When drawing it, make sure you feel like it is a part of the intention. This means taking a bit of automatic writing / thinking and just "allowing" the pen to draw it for you
  4. Continuously think of the intent, belief, visual imagery of the intent, and play out the intent in your head whilst drawing.
  5. Feel your energy escape onto the page as you feel which one is right to you. It's like chipping away at marble to make a fabulous sculpture.
  6. When charging, make sure you do a proper energetic transfer method. I've outlined in one of those hypersigil threads. I also would suggest combining all your thoughts of the sigil, feelings about what happens when it's completely done, scenery from the finished manifestation, etc.
  7. I do not throw away my sigils, nor burn them, nor even jack off on them. Those waste the sigils energy and I feel they actually take away from the overall power.

Thanks!
